en:
Chapter Four: “A New Life.”

And slowly, the years settled, one upon another.

My days had found their colors. Laughing beneath the spring sunlight through the leaves, looking up at summer thunderheads. Loving autumn's falling leaves, delighting in winter's rare covering of snow.

As those days repeated, changes in my surroundings accumulated. Changes that were far from small.

The servants from Gospel House came and went.

It wasn't like school, with grades, so no strict rule said who had to leave after how many years. Each servant and their circumstances decided when to “graduate” from Rokkenjima.

Some, who found the place entirely wrong for them, couldn't last even three days.

Life on Rokkenjima was harsh. Gospel House was strict too, of course, but Rokkenjima had many rules of its own, and Natsuhi's supervision of the servants was severe.

Often, they must have felt confined. They weighed that confinement against their wages and chose their own time to graduate.

Sometimes, the Ushiromiya family would arrange another job and encourage them to spread their wings in a new chapter of their lives.

That cycle usually took two or three years. No one had decided it, but it had become a goal for their service, an unspoken rule.

I was outside that rule too. Still attending school on Niijima, still living as a servant...

That year, a whole group of Gospel House servants decided to leave. It wasn't unusual for servants who were friends to leave together.

Leaving only me behind, all my companions from Gospel House graduated from the island at once...

I hadn't been close to them. Quite the opposite. They kept calling me Yasu, Yasu, treating me as half-trained no matter how much time passed. It was unpleasant.

Even when someone new arrived, the older servants filled their ears with stories about how Yasu was always losing things. New companions came, and nothing became any more pleasant.

Now, those unpleasant seniors, peers, and juniors were all leaving together.

The Ushiromiya family didn't pursue anyone who left. Adults were easier to employ as servants in the first place. The Gospel House servants were only accepted as trainees.

So no one asked them to stay. All the servants besides me left at once...

第四章。“新しき日々”。　そして年月はゆっくりと降り積もる。　彩を得た我が日々は、春の木漏れ日に笑い、夏に入道雲を見上げ、秋には落ちる木の葉を愛で、冬は稀なる雪化粧を楽しむ。　そんな日々が繰り返されるうちに、決して小さくない環境の変化が重なっていった。　それは、福音の家より来た使用人たちの入れ替わりである。　学校のように学年があるわけではないので、誰が何年で辞めると、厳密に決まっているわけではない。　何年で六軒島を“卒業”するかは、使用人たち個々人と環境が判断することなのである。　よほど環境が合わない使用人なら、来て３日ともたない者もいる。　何しろ、六軒島での生活は厳しい。　福音の家ももちろん厳しいが、六軒島ならではの決まりごとも多く、使用人たちを統括する夏妃の指導も厳しい。窮屈に感じることも多いだろう。　その窮屈さと給金を秤に掛け、彼らは自ら、卒業の時期を判断するのである。　また、時には右代宮家の方から、就職先の斡旋があり、新しいステージへ羽ばたくよう勧められることもある。　そのサイクルは、大抵は２～３年程度。
　誰が決めたわけではないが、それが彼らの勤続の、一つの目標であり、暗黙のルールとなっていた。　しかし、我はそのルールからも外れていた。　未だ、新島の学校に通い続けながら、使用人生活を続けている......。　その年、ごっそりと福音の家の使用人たちが辞めることとなった。
　仲の良い使用人たちが、連れ立って同時に辞めることは珍しくなかった。　我だけを残し、福音の家から来た仲間たちは一斉に、この島から卒業していった...。　我は、別に彼らと仲が良かったわけではない。　むしろ、ヤスヤスと呼ばれ、いつまで経っても半人前扱いだったので、不愉快なくらいだった。　せっかく後輩が入ってきても、先輩たちが私のことを、ヤスはよく物をなくして云々と吹き込んだため、新しい仲間が来ても不愉快なままだったのだ。　その、不愉快な先輩も同輩も後輩も、一度に辞めることとなった。　右代宮家は去る者を追わない。
　そもそも、使用人としては、大人の方が使いやすい。　あくまでも福音の家の使用人は、研修として受け容れているだけだ。
　だから、誰も引き止めず、私以外の使用人たちは、一度に辞めた......。

ja: 「じゃーね、ヤス。あんた、物を無くしたりするんじゃないわよ」「……もう、無くしたりなんかしてません」「ふんっ。じゃーね。奥様の言うこと、よく聞くのよ。後から来る仲間に迷惑掛けるんじゃないわよ」「……未だに謎よね。どうしてヤスはここに推薦されたの？」「それを言ったら、未だに奥様がヤスの勤務を認めてる方が意外だわ」「逃げ出さない分だけ、根性があるってもんだ。しっかりな、ヤ・ス」「わ、私、……ヤスって呼ばれるの、嫌いです…」
en:
“Bye, Yasu. Don't go losing things.”

“...I don't lose them anymore.”

“Hmph. Bye, then. Listen to Madam. Don't make trouble for the next people who come.”

“...Still a mystery, isn't it? Why was Yasu recommended here?”

“Speaking of mysteries, it's more surprising Madam still lets Yasu work here.”

“Sticking it out without running away takes guts, at least. Hang in there, Ya-su.”

“I-I ...don't like being called Yasu...”

en:
At the very end, ...I finally managed to say the one thing I'd wanted to say to them.

But they hardly noticed. They gathered their luggage and filed out...

rows.enText: “...You never did make friends with them.”
rows.jaText: 「……みんなとは、ついにお友達になれなかったね」

ja: 「なりたくもなかったし」

rows.enText: “I didn't want to.”
rows.jaText: 「なりたくもなかったし」

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「うん。向こうもそうだったろうし、お相子だね。あの人たちのことは、もう忘れちゃおう。もう、お互い、何の関わりもない。だから、心に留める必要もない」
en: “No. They probably didn't want to either, so you're even. Let's forget them. You have nothing to do with each other anymore. No reason to keep them in your heart.”
rows.enText: “No. They probably didn't want to either, so you're even. Let's forget them. You have nothing to do with each other anymore. No reason to keep them in your heart.”

ja: 「…………うん。……そうだね」

rows.enText: “...Mm. ... You're right.”
rows.jaText: 「…………うん。……そうだね」

ja: ちょっとだけ、悔しかった。最後まで彼女らに、私がしっかり一人前になったことを、認めてもらえなかった。
en: It frustrated me a little. Right to the end, they had never acknowledged that I'd become fully capable.
rows.enText: It frustrated me a little. Right to the end, they had never acknowledged that I'd become fully capable.
rows.jaText: ちょっとだけ、悔しかった。最後まで彼女らに、私がしっかり一人前になったことを、認めてもらえなかった。

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「人は、最初の印象をいつまでも引き摺る生き物だからね。……だから仕方がない。あなたがどんなに素晴らしい人間に成長しても、彼女らはきっと、いつまでもヤスと呼び続けて、あなたを馬鹿にしたと思うもの。そんな人たちに認めさせようと思うなんて、全然意味のないことなんだよ」
en: “People carry their first impressions around forever. ...It can't be helped. However wonderful a person you grew into, I'm sure they'd have kept calling you Yasu and mocking you. Trying to make people like that accept you is pointless.”
rows.enText: “People carry their first impressions around forever. ...It can't be helped. However wonderful a person you grew into, I'm sure they'd have kept calling you Yasu and mocking you. Trying to make people like that accept you is pointless.”

ja: 「……そうだね。うん、紗音の言う通り。もう、あの人たちのことは綺麗さっぱり忘れるよ」
en: “...You're right. Yes, Shannon. I'll forget them, completely.”
rows.enText: “...You're right. Yes, Shannon. I'll forget them, completely.”
rows.jaText: 「……そうだね。うん、紗音の言う通り。もう、あの人たちのことは綺麗さっぱり忘れるよ」

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「それがいいよ。あなたには私や熊沢さんなどの、素敵な友達がいるじゃない。そして、新しい使用人の人たちの前では、今度は一人前の姿を見せてあげればいい」
en: “That's best. You have lovely friends, like me and Kumasawa. And this time, show the new servants how capable you are.”
rows.enText: “That's best. You have lovely friends, like me and Kumasawa. And this time, show the new servants how capable you are.”

ja: まったく、紗音の言う通りだった。私は、あの蜘蛛の糸のまじないの鍵を高々と掲げたあの日以来の、誇らしげな気持ちを取り戻す。……福音の家の使用人たちの中で、自分が一番の古参となったのだ。新しく来る使用人は、相変わらず私よりも年上だろうけれど。私が、先輩として色々教えなきゃ。源次さまも、これからは先輩として指導するようにと言ってくれてた…。うん。……がんばろう。
en:
Shannon was entirely right.

I felt proud again, as I had on the day I'd held high the key with its spider's-thread spell.

...Now I was the longest-serving of the Gospel House servants. The newcomers would still be older than me, probably. But I would be their senior. I would have to teach them all sorts of things.

Master Genji had told me to guide them as their senior from now on...

Yes. ...I'd do my best.

The newcomers would still be older than me, probably. But I would be their senior. I would have to teach them all sorts of things. Master Genji had told me to guide them as their senior from now on... Yes. ...I'd do my best.

ja: 「その意気だね。一緒にがんばろう」
en: “That's the spirit. Let's do our best together.”
rows.enText: “That's the spirit. Let's do our best together.”
rows.jaText: 「その意気だね。一緒にがんばろう」

ja: 「うん！」
en: “Yes!”
rows.enText: “Yes!”
rows.jaText: 「うん！」

“My name is Asne. I look forward to working with you.”

“I'm Belne! Looking forward to working with you!”

en:
.....................

The newcomers ...seemed, somehow, rather frivolous.

When I'd first come to the Ushiromiya family, I'd been terribly nervous. I couldn't sense the slightest nervousness in them...

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「えぇ。基本的には成績が優秀で、品行方正な子が選ばれます」
en: “Yes. Basically, the children chosen have excellent grades and good conduct.”

en: “How do they choose? Who chooses?”
rows.enText: “How do they choose? Who chooses?”
rows.jaText: 「どうやって選ぶの？　誰が選ぶの？」

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「理事の先生方が来て、面接をされるんです。他にも、日頃の素行とか…」
en: “The directors come and interview us. They consider our everyday conduct too...”
rows.enText: “The directors come and interview us. They consider our everyday conduct too...”
rows.jaText: 「理事の先生方が来て、面接をされるんです。他にも、日頃の素行とか…」

rows.speaker: Furfur
ja: 「じゃあ！　先生の前でだけいい子ぶってても、合格できちゃうってことも？」
en: “So! Could someone pass by acting good only when the teachers are looking?”
rows.enText: “So! Could someone pass by acting good only when the teachers are looking?”

rows.enText: “...Well, um, ... if the teachers see them and judge them to be good, they might pass...”

en:
“The children from Gospel House were always distinctive individuals. Daily life as servants polished them, until they became fine people, worthy of the name of Ushiromiya family servant.”

“But it was the senior servants' task to bring that about. ...Now that I alone was experienced, I had the responsibility of guiding them well.”

“But one key quietly slipped away without a sound. ...That was when I first realized. This wasn't a prank because Yasu was lashing out. ...It was something, ...something more dangerous...”

en:
“In my... ...locker.”

“You're careless, Belne... Maybe you took just that key off, put it in your locker, and forgot...?”

“Why would I take just that key off the ring?! Asne, have you ever taken a key off one, or put one back?! I tried it myself. It's so stiff! You wouldn't do it without a reason! There'd be no point! Am I sleepwalking?! Are you saying I can't even remember what I've done?!”

“I'm stupid, but not that stupid! I don't forget my own actions like that! And the key was definitely there when I went into the room! If it wasn't, how did I unlock the door?!” “...So ... without making any noise, just ... slipping it off, ...Yasu must have managed to take the key and hide it in your locker...”

“I thought so too, at first! I went for Yasu, said, Don't you mess with me! But even as I said it, I was thinking. Isn't this really strange?!”

“Because all that day, we were going around the rooms with Yasu, weren't we?! There was never enough of an opening to rattle a key off the ring! Yasu couldn't do it! Nobody could! Taking off just one key, without a sound, in that little moment!”

“M-maybe there was already one master key missing when you got them...”

“I'm telling you!! The key was there at first! I unlocked the room! So it was definitely there! ...Then we went in! And because I'm stupid, I hate keys jangling, so I just put them down on the bed...!”

“...Asne wouldn't believe anything I said. So after a while, I stopped going to her and ...told Yasu about it instead. I thought it was your prank, but it definitely isn't you. Something, ...something strange is doing this to us!”

However often I warned her, she wouldn't change. She called me Yasu, Yasu, mocked me. Nothing I said could make her listen...

Why wouldn't she listen to me...?

You mustn't put things down carelessly. Leave an opening, and the witch will play pranks and make you suffer...

en:
A chill rose from my feet, like needles of frost, spreading through my body like an electric shock.

From that instant, ...I could no longer move any part of my body by my own will.

As with a sudden power outage, when you can only stand helpless and dazed, I could only accept that I'd lost control of my body...

Every cell in me tingled, as though bubbling. ...The feeling of my flesh being remade, in an instant, into someone else's.

...Using my body as a vessel, ...the witch Beatrice was coming back to life, briefly. I could feel it...

My mind went blank in an instant. Thought stopped.

Something unknown. Indescribable. ...A feeling I had never known.

My mind was blank. I could think of nothing. Dazed, ...I could only give my soul to the feeling traveling from my feet, through my body, and out through my fingertips.

At last, I understood. This was ... what it meant ... to use magic...

ja: 私の指が、操り人形のように動き、魔法を奏でるかのように踊る。自分の意思によらずに体が動くことは、こんなにもくすぐったいことなのか…。ベアトが操り糸を手繰るように指を立てると、ベッドの上に放り出されている鍵束が、ひょっこりと起き上がる。……鐘音さんは、気付かない。……明日音さんも、気付かない。お部屋のお掃除をしながら、楽しそうなおしゃべりに夢中になっている…。その二人の後に魔女がいて、今まさに魔法の力を振るおうとしているなんて、夢にも思わないだろう。まさか、自分たちの背中で、……鍵束がダンスを踊っているなんて、想像も出来ないだろう。それはまるで、幼い頃にテレビで見た、アニメのおとぎ話のよう。楽しそうに跳ねて、くるくるとダンスを踊る様は、まるで鍵束が自らの意思でそうしているかのように見える。ぞわぞわと、……指先を通して、鍵束とダンスを踊るという楽しさが、私の全身に染み渡った…。そう、これは、快楽なのだ……。私は全身を魔女に委ねながら呆然と、……魔法という、未知の快楽に、身を委ねる他なかった……。
en:
My fingers moved like a puppet's, dancing as though magic were music.

Could it really tickle this much, having your body move without your will...?

When Beato raised my fingers as though drawing on puppet strings, the keys abandoned on the bed popped upright.

...Belne didn't notice. ...Asne didn't notice either. Cleaning the room, they were absorbed in their cheerful conversation...

They would never dream a witch stood behind them, about to wield magic. They could never imagine ... the keys dancing behind their backs.

Like an animated fairy tale I'd watched on television when I was little. Happily hopping and whirling, they looked as though they were dancing of their own will.

Tingling, ...through my fingertips, the joy of dancing with the keys spread through my whole body...

Yes. This was pleasure...

Giving my whole body to the witch, dazed, ...I could only surrender to that unknown pleasure called magic...

ベアトが指を鳴らすと、鍵はポンと爆ぜて、黄金の蝶に姿を変える。……黄金の蝶…？そうか、お館様に黄金を授けた黄金の魔女だから、黄金なのか。そして、蜘蛛の糸を嫌がるのは蝶。……だから、黄金の、蝶。黄金の蝶は、魔女ベアトリーチェの、眷属なのだ……。ふわりと、空中を舞った後、ポンと黄金の鱗粉を弾けさせて消える。そして、消えた鍵は、……鐘音さんのロッカーの中に……。それはここではない、更衣室のロッカーの話なのに、その様子がありありと理解できた。それは、視覚でも感触でもない。
五感では説明の出来ない、心の中のもう一つの感触。
今日までに一度も感じたことのない、まったく新しい感触。つまり、魔法という、まったくの未知の概念。
恍惚とする他ない、まったくの未知の、快楽。
en:
Beato snapped my fingers. The key popped and became a golden butterfly.

...A golden butterfly...?

Of course. Gold, because she was the Golden Witch who'd given gold to the Master. And butterflies didn't like spider's threads.

...So, a golden butterfly. Golden butterflies were the familiars of the witch Beatrice...

It fluttered lightly in the air, then popped in a burst of golden wing dust and vanished.

And the vanished key ...was inside Belne's locker...

Not here. In the changing room. Yet I could understand it vividly.

It wasn't sight or touch. Another feeling within my heart, which the five senses could not explain. An entirely new feeling, one I'd never felt before today.

In other words, an entirely unknown idea. Magic. An entirely unknown pleasure that could only leave me enraptured.

That pleasure. That excitement. ...Still lingering faintly in my fingers...

en:
Suddenly saying that, Belne turned and snatched the keys she'd tossed onto the bed.

Apparently, she'd noticed me staring at them.

ja: 「まーたヤスに、鍵をこんなところに放り出さないでーって怒られるところでしたー。私、置きっ放しにして忘れたりなんかー、しませんからー」
en: “Almost got told off by Yasu again. Don't leave your keys lying around! I don't leave things and forget them, you know.”
rows.enText: “Almost got told off by Yasu again. Don't leave your keys lying around! I don't leave things and forget them, you know.”

ja: と、にやりと笑いながら、鍵束をポケットに戻す。しかし、まだ気付いていない。鍵が一本だけ、……ほんのちょっと油断した間に消えているなんて、想像もしないだろう…。それはニンゲンには、容易に出来ることではない。……でも、魔法なら。鍵たちとダンスを踊り、ポンっと蝶が爆ぜるだけで、……姿を消せてしまう。
en:
Grinning, she put the keys in her pocket.

But she hadn't noticed yet. She would never imagine ...one key had disappeared while she'd let her guard down for that little moment.

Something a human could not easily do. ...But with magic. Dance with the keys, a butterfly pops, ...and it vanishes.

“Tools, okay! Keys, okay! See? Everything's fine!”

“Y-yes, everything's fine... Let's go to the next room. ...Oh, ...Belne. Please ...lock this one.”

ja: ………本当に、……鐘音さんの鍵は、……魔法で消えたの？あの楽しげな魔法は、私だけの白昼夢では……？それを認めるのが怖くて、……私は、試す。
en:
...Had Belne's key really ... disappeared through magic?

Had that happy magic only been my own daydream...?

Afraid to accept that, ...I tested it.

“........................ ...Huh...”

“What's up? What are you doing?”

“...Huh. ...Huh, huh. ...What is this? Seriously?”

“What's wrong...?”

“...Not this one. ...Not this one. ...Hm? Huh?”

“What's wrong? Want me to lock it?”

“I-I don't get it. What is this? ...The master key's gone. Just the master key's gone. Wh-why...?! It's so solid. It couldn't have come off...!”

ja: 私の指先に、ぞくりと。……あの、ダンスを踊った時のぞわぞわした感触が、わずかに蘇るのを感じた……。
en: A shiver at my fingertips. ...A faint return of that tingling feeling from when we'd danced...
rows.enText: A shiver at my fingertips. ...A faint return of that tingling feeling from when we'd danced...

夜。……寮の自室のベッドで天井を眺めながら、……自分の両手を見た。眠れない。まだ指先に、……あの、鍵束とダンスを踊った時のわくわくが、残っている…。あれは、……ベアトリーチェにとっては、……魔女にとっては、……当り前のことだったのだろうか。…………ベアトリーチェという、魔女の友人がいる。
彼女は不思議な魔法で、いつも私に悪戯をしていた。それをいつも見せられてきたから、………私は魔法を、知っているつもりだった。しかし今日。……彼女は私の体に憑依し、……私の体で魔法を使った。そこで初めて知った魔法の感触は、……未だに私の心を虜にしている。まったく未知の、初めて知る快楽だった。だって……。指先を動かすと自在に、………鍵が踊ったのだ。
ニンゲンには出来ない、不思議な不思議な、魔法の奇跡。まだ、……興奮が冷めない…。……………………。
en:
Night.

...On the bed in my dorm room, gazing at the ceiling, ...I looked at both my hands.

I couldn't sleep. Still in my fingertips, ...the excitement of dancing with the keys remained... Was that ...an ordinary thing ... for Beatrice, ...for a witch...?

...I had a witch for a friend. Beatrice. She was always using strange magic to play pranks on me.

I'd watched her do it all this time, so ...I'd thought I knew magic.

But today. ...She'd possessed my body, ...and used magic through it.

The feeling of magic I'd first known then ...still held my heart captive.

An utterly unknown pleasure. One I had never known before. Because... When my fingertips moved, ... the keys danced, just as I wished. A strange, strange miracle of magic, impossible for a human.

Still, ...the excitement hadn't faded...

........................

ja: 紗音はまだ起きていた。紗音はいつも早寝早起き。夜は早めに休んで、一日の疲れを翌日に残さない。……使用人として憧れるべき、模範的な生活だった。……紗音のような、……みんなに愛され、尊敬される使用人になりたかったら、………そうでなくてはいけない。でも、私はそうなれる自信が、……もう、なかった。
en:
Shannon was still awake. She always went to bed early and rose early. She rested early at night so she wouldn't carry one day's fatigue into the next.

...The model of a servant's life. Something to aspire to.

...If I wanted to become a servant like Shannon, ...loved and respected by everyone, ...I had to live that way.

But now ...I no longer believed I could.

en: “At Gospel House, you were kind to everyone, and loved. ...You always played with me. You were my only friend. And in the Ushiromiya mansion, a wonderful, lovely servant, doing every job gracefully, without a mistake. My dream. My goal. ...That was you.”

en: “Yes. ... Let's do our best together. You know what they say. Even a stone grows warm if you sit on it for three years. Everyone's accepting you more and more. So let's try to become wonderful servants together.”

rows.enText: “A w-witch...? ...What are you talking about...?”

rows.enText: “That's, ...um, ...what...?”

en:
Shannon was bewildered. Naturally.

...If I'd been talking about leaving my job, she could have understood. But suddenly saying I dreamed of becoming a witch would leave her speechless...

“Like discovering a world I hadn't known. ...Like I'd lived only in darkness, thinking I knew everything about the world, and then discovered light for the first time. Saw the world. That joy. ...That excitement.”

ja:
あの時、ベアトは私の指を介して、鍵束とダンスを踊り、鍵を一本、蝶に変えてロッカーの中に隠しただけだった。でも、私の体は理解していた。もし、別の指の動かし方をしていたら、ダンスでなく、宙を羽ばたかせることも、蝶でなく、トカゲに変えてベッドを駆け回ることも、……何でも出来た。確かにベアトリーチェの魔力は未だ弱い。反魔法の毒素を持つ鐘音さんたちが背中を向けてくれた束の間の世界の出来事。しかし、その束の間の世界では、何でも出来た。
ベアトは、たまたま、躍らせて、蝶にしただけ。
でも、もしも望んだなら、他のことも何でも出来た！あの自由な、何の制約もない力の無限の感触。
まだこの指先に残ってる。感触だけでなく、魔力の欠片がわずかほどでも残っていたりはしないだろうか…？わかる。残ってる。………まだちょっとだけ、感触と共に残ってる。出来る。……私にもまだ、………出来る……。
en:
Then, Beato had only danced with the keys through my fingers, turned one into a butterfly, and hidden it in the locker.

But my body understood.

With another movement of my fingers, instead of dancing, I could have made it fly. Instead of a butterfly, a lizard, running around the bed. ...Anything was possible.

Certainly, Beatrice's magic was still weak. It had happened in the brief world when Belne and the others, with their anti-magic toxin, had turned their backs.

But in that brief world, anything was possible. Beato had happened to make it dance, and then become a butterfly. But if she'd wished, she could have done anything else!

That feeling of infinite power, free, with no restraints. Still in these fingertips.

Perhaps, along with the feeling, a tiny fragment of magic remained...?

I knew. It was there. ...Just a little, still there, with the feeling.

I could. ...Even I could ...still do it...

When I ...gently opened them, like a flower bud, ...there was a single grain of glittering gold.

紗音には、その輝きの意味するものが、わからない。手の平より光が生まれるわけがない。なのに生まれたという奇跡を目の当たりにしてさえ、……それが何か、理解できずにいる。ただ呆然とし、……ぽかんと開いた口を、閉じることも忘れていた。でも、私にとってそれは、……確かに指先にまだ残る感触の、再現。黄金の粒は、……ふわっと広がり、……小さな、黄金の蝶に姿を変える。それは、ぱたぱたと羽ばたき、ティンカーベルのように、黄金の鱗粉を散らす。紗音には、ただ、黄金の蝶が羽ばたいているようにしか見えないだろう。……もちろんそれさえも、彼女には理解し難い奇跡なのだが。しかし私にはそれは、……蝶に姿を変えての、空中飛行。
私は黄金の蝶を、自在に操っているのだ。操り糸でよたよたとではない。
……私の意志で羽ばたき、舞い、空中を自在に、遊ぶ。蝶という分身を通しての、私の空中散歩。小さな部屋の闇を黄金の輝きで切り裂き、自在に宙を舞う、喜び。……恍惚とした、悦楽。……しかし、指先の中のその感触が、少しずつ薄れていく。指の中にわずかに残っていた魔法の鱗粉が、無くなるのがわかった。やがて黄金の蝶は、線香花火が消えてしまうかのように、最後には小さく瞬き、ぽとりと黄金の粒になって落ちて、そして跡形もなく消え去った……。
en:
Shannon didn't understand what the light meant. Light could not be born from a palm. Even seeing that impossible miracle before her eyes, ... she couldn't understand what it was.

She only stared, ...forgetting even to close her open mouth. But for me, ... it recreated the feeling I knew was still in my fingertips. The golden grain ... spread softly, ... taking the form of a small golden butterfly.

It fluttered, scattering golden wing dust like Tinker Bell.

To Shannon, it would only look like a golden butterfly fluttering. ...Of course, even that was a miracle difficult for her to understand.

But to me, ...it was flight through the air in a butterfly's form. I was controlling the golden butterfly however I wished.

Not a clumsy movement on puppet strings. ...It beat its wings with my will, danced, played freely in the air.

My walk through the sky, through that other self called a butterfly. The joy of slicing the little room's darkness with golden light, dancing freely in the air.

...Enraptured delight.

...But slowly, the feeling in my fingertips faded. I could feel the last dust of magic in my fingers running out.

At last, like a little sparkler burning out, the golden butterfly gave one final flicker. It dropped as a grain of gold, then vanished without a trace...

“I see. Then, after awakening to magic, Beatrice becomes my equal and my friend. So I shall be a friend rather like an older sister.”

“Yes. I'll inherit it.”

“Yeah. ...No. ...Indeed!”

“Well. I am a witch all in red. Why not choose a mood built around another color?”

“...When Beatrice wanders the mansion at night, she often appears as a white figure.”

“The usual color for a ghost, then.” “A witch ... in a white dress... ...I'll try bringing the image together.”

ja: 「安心せよ、必ず立派な名前を考えてやろうぞ！　それよりまず、考えたいことがある。それは妾の使う魔法のイメージである！」「物を隠したり、別の場所に瞬間移動させる魔法はそなたのイメージだ。だから、妾も妾に相応しい魔法のイメージを考えねばな。……魔法を使う時、黄金の蝶が飛び交う。そこは譲れぬぞ…！」
en:
“Have no fear. I shall think of a splendid name for you! But first, there is something else I wish to consider. The form my magic shall take!”

“Hiding things, moving them instantly elsewhere, that is your style of magic. So I must imagine a style worthy of me. ...When magic is used, golden butterflies fly. I will not yield that...!”
rows.enText: “Have no fear. I shall think of a splendid name for you! But first, there is something else I wish to consider. The form my magic shall take!” “Hiding things, moving them instantly elsewhere, that is your style of magic. So I must imagine a style worthy of me. ...When magic is used, golden butterflies fly. I will not yield that...!”

ja: 「くす。素敵ね。それこそ、まさに黄金の魔女。……じゃあ、蜘蛛の糸が苦手で、社に納められてる霊鏡が苦手で、という弱点もあなたに？」
en: “Hee. Lovely. Exactly what the Golden Witch should have. ...Then do the weaknesses become yours too? Spider's threads, the sacred mirror kept in the shrine?”
rows.enText: “Hee. Lovely. Exactly what the Golden Witch should have. ...Then do the weaknesses become yours too? Spider's threads, the sacred mirror kept in the shrine?”
rows.jaText: 「くす。素敵ね。それこそ、まさに黄金の魔女。……じゃあ、蜘蛛の糸が苦手で、社に納められてる霊鏡が苦手で、という弱点もあなたに？」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「ふむ。万能の魔女にも、何かささやかな弱点があった方が面白いというもの。では、こうしよう。蜘蛛の糸に触れたら火傷をするということとする」
en: “Mm. Even an all-powerful witch is more interesting with some little weakness. Let us make it this. Touch a spider's thread, and I am burned.”
rows.enText: “Mm. Even an all-powerful witch is more interesting with some little weakness. Let us make it this. Touch a spider's thread, and I am burned.”
rows.jaText: 「ふむ。万能の魔女にも、何かささやかな弱点があった方が面白いというもの。では、こうしよう。蜘蛛の糸に触れたら火傷をするということとする」

ja:
すぅっと、銀色の蜘蛛が静かに、上から下に横切っていく。その後に軌跡として残る銀色の糸に、新しき姿を得たベアトがすっと触れる。すると、……小さく肉の焼ける音がして、ベアトの指先には一文字の火傷が残った。ベアトリーチェは、蜘蛛の糸が苦手。
熊沢さんが言ってた、六軒島の悪霊の弱点。その悪霊の力を得て、魔女ベアトリーチェは復活をしているから、弱点も引き継いでしまっているのだ。同様に、霊鏡も弱点。……しかし、社の霊鏡なんて、そうそう妾の前には現れないだろう。ちょっと面白くない。
en:
A silver spider quietly descended past us, leaving a silver thread behind.

Beato, in her new form, gently touched it.

Then ...the faint sizzle of flesh. A straight-line burn remained across her fingertip.

Beatrice was vulnerable to spider's threads. The weakness of Rokkenjima's evil spirit, which Kumasawa had spoken of.

The witch Beatrice had returned to life through that evil spirit's power, so she had inherited its weakness too.

Likewise, the sacred mirror was a weakness.

...But a sacred mirror from the shrine wasn't likely to appear before me very often. A little dull.

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「………では、霊力のある鏡は無論のこと、鏡自体も苦手ということにしよう」
en: “...Then let us say I dislike mirrors themselves, as well as those with spiritual power.”
rows.enText: “...Then let us say I dislike mirrors themselves, as well as those with spiritual power.”
rows.jaText: 「………では、霊力のある鏡は無論のこと、鏡自体も苦手ということにしよう」

ja: 「鏡って魔力があるってよく言うものね。いいんじゃない？　如何にも魔女っぽい感じ」
en: “People often say mirrors hold magic, after all. Why not? It sounds exactly like a witch.”
rows.enText: “People often say mirrors hold magic, after all. Why not? It sounds exactly like a witch.”
rows.jaText: 「鏡って魔力があるってよく言うものね。いいんじゃない？　如何にも魔女っぽい感じ」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「鏡を見ると、魔力が吸い取られる感じがするので、苦手、ということにしよう。うむ、面白そうだ」
en: “Looking in a mirror feels as though my magic is being drawn away. So I dislike them. Yes. Interesting.”
rows.enText: “Looking in a mirror feels as though my magic is being drawn away. So I dislike them. Yes. Interesting.”
rows.jaText: 「鏡を見ると、魔力が吸い取られる感じがするので、苦手、ということにしよう。うむ、面白そうだ」

ja: ……よくよく考えれば。そんな設定などなくとも、私は鏡が苦手。私が誰になろうとも、憧れようとも、……鏡に映るのは、いつも無残なくらいに情けなく現実的な、
ヤス
i
の顔。みすぼらしい自分の現実を、無理やり突きつける鏡は、いつだって、私の苦手なもの。うん。……鏡は、嫌い。……みすぼらしい自分なんか、見たく、ない。
en:
...Thinking about it carefully.

Even without such a rule, I disliked mirrors. Whoever I became, whoever I dreamed of being, ... what the mirror reflected was always ...
Yasu
i

's face. Pitiful, cruelly real.

A mirror forced the shabby truth of myself upon me. I had always hated that.

Yes. ...I hated mirrors. ...I didn't want ... to see ... my shabby self.

Pitiful, cruelly real. A mirror forced the shabby truth of myself upon me. I had always hated that. Yes. ...I hated mirrors. ...I didn't want ... to see ... my shabby self.

ja: 「一度に何もかも決めなくていいわ。世界を、ゆっくりと作り上げていくのだって、とても楽しいのだから」
en: “You don't have to decide everything at once. Slowly building the world is a pleasure too.”
rows.enText: “You don't have to decide everything at once. Slowly building the world is a pleasure too.”
rows.jaText: 「一度に何もかも決めなくていいわ。世界を、ゆっくりと作り上げていくのだって、とても楽しいのだから」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「うむ。わかっている。ゆっくりと、魔女の生活を楽しみながら、妾の世界を膨らませてゆこうぞ」
en: “Mm. I know. Let us slowly expand my world, enjoying life as a witch.”
rows.enText: “Mm. I know. Let us slowly expand my world, enjoying life as a witch.”
rows.jaText: 「うむ。わかっている。ゆっくりと、魔女の生活を楽しみながら、妾の世界を膨らませてゆこうぞ」

ja: 「あの狭くて暗い部屋はもう、あんたの寝床じゃないわね」
en: “That cramped, dark room isn't your bedroom anymore, is it?”
rows.enText: “That cramped, dark room isn't your bedroom anymore, is it?”
rows.jaText: 「あの狭くて暗い部屋はもう、あんたの寝床じゃないわね」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「ふむ。妾こそは黄金の魔女！　六軒島の夜の支配者なれば、夜の屋敷は妾のもの。妾の住まうべきは屋敷ではないか」
en: “Mm. I am the Golden Witch! Ruler of Rokkenjima's night. The mansion at night is mine. So surely I should live in the mansion.”
rows.enText: “Mm. I am the Golden Witch! Ruler of Rokkenjima's night. The mansion at night is mine. So surely I should live in the mansion.”
rows.jaText: 「ふむ。妾こそは黄金の魔女！　六軒島の夜の支配者なれば、夜の屋敷は妾のもの。妾の住まうべきは屋敷ではないか」

rows.speaker: Zepar
ja: 「ベアトリーチェの部屋？　はは、決まってるじゃないか！」
en: “Beatrice's room? Ha! Isn't it obvious?!”
rows.enText: “Beatrice's room? Ha! Isn't it obvious?!”
rows.jaText: 「ベアトリーチェの部屋？　はは、決まってるじゃないか！」

rows.speaker: Furfur
ja: 「えぇ、そうね！　お屋敷の２階の、あの素敵な部屋……」
en: “Yes, of course! That lovely room on the mansion's second floor...”
rows.enText: “Yes, of course! That lovely room on the mansion's second floor...”
rows.jaText: 「えぇ、そうね！　お屋敷の２階の、あの素敵な部屋……」

rows.speaker: Zepar
ja: 「魔女の貴賓室こそ、ベアトリーチェの部屋じゃないか！」
en: “The witch's special guestroom! Isn't that Beatrice's room?!”
rows.enText: “The witch's special guestroom! Isn't that Beatrice's room?!”
rows.jaText: 「魔女の貴賓室こそ、ベアトリーチェの部屋じゃないか！」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「おお、そうであったな。今宵より、妾が住まうは夜の屋敷のあの部屋ではないか…！　これはうっかりしていた、ははは、くっはははははははは…！！」
en: “Oh, so it is. From tonight, that room in the nighttime mansion is my home...! Careless of me. Hahaha, heh hahahahahaha...!!”
rows.enText: “Oh, so it is. From tonight, that room in the nighttime mansion is my home...! Careless of me. Hahaha, heh hahahahahaha...!!”
rows.jaText: 「おお、そうであったな。今宵より、妾が住まうは夜の屋敷のあの部屋ではないか…！　これはうっかりしていた、ははは、くっはははははははは…！！」

ja: 「じゃあ、行きましょ、ベアト。魔女が二人、お茶をするなら、あんな狭い部屋じゃなくて、相応しい素敵な部屋でするべきだわ」
en: “Let's go, Beato. If two witches are having tea, it should be in a lovely room worthy of us, not some little cramped room.”
rows.enText: “Let's go, Beato. If two witches are having tea, it should be in a lovely room worthy of us, not some little cramped room.”
rows.jaText: 「じゃあ、行きましょ、ベアト。魔女が二人、お茶をするなら、あんな狭い部屋じゃなくて、相応しい素敵な部屋でするべきだわ」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「そうであるな。友人を招いて茶を振舞うには、あの部屋は粗末が過ぎる。部屋を変えよう。行こうではないか、我が友よ…！」
en: “Indeed. That room is too shabby for inviting a friend to tea. Let us change rooms. Come, my friend...!”
rows.enText: “Indeed. That room is too shabby for inviting a friend to tea. Let us change rooms. Come, my friend...!”
rows.jaText: 「そうであるな。友人を招いて茶を振舞うには、あの部屋は粗末が過ぎる。部屋を変えよう。行こうではないか、我が友よ…！」

ja: 「………紗音とは、お別れね」
en: “...Goodbye to Shannon, then.”
rows.enText: “...Goodbye to Shannon, then.”
rows.jaText: 「………紗音とは、お別れね」

ja: 足元を見下ろすと、……はるか眼下に、寮の自分の部屋が見える。私が横になっているベッドに駆け寄り、待って、と言ったまま時間が止まり、人形のように硬直している紗音が見える。この高みから見下ろすと、それはまるで、小さな人形とそのお家みたいだ…。
en:
Looking down, ...far below my feet, I could see my dorm room.

Shannon had rushed to the bed where I lay. Time had stopped as she said, Wait. She was stiff as a doll.

From this height, it looked like a little doll and her little house...
rows.enText: Looking down, ...far below my feet, I could see my dorm room. Shannon had rushed to the bed where I lay. Time had stopped as she said, Wait. She was stiff as a doll. From this height, it looked like a little doll and her little house...
rows.jaText: 足元を見下ろすと、……はるか眼下に、寮の自分の部屋が見える。私が横になっているベッドに駆け寄り、待って、と言ったまま時間が止まり、人形のように硬直している紗音が見える。この高みから見下ろすと、それはまるで、小さな人形とそのお家みたいだ…。

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 「さらばだ、紗音。……ニンゲンとして、そなたを目標に、そなたと友情を育みながらの日々も、楽しいものであったぞ。…もし妾が、魔法の悦楽を知ることなく、魔女に開眼することがなかったなら、それはこれからも変わらなかったであろうな」
en: “Farewell, Shannon. ...My human days were happy too, with you as my goal, nurturing our friendship. ...Had I never known the pleasure of magic, never awakened as a witch, that would have continued.”
rows.enText: “Farewell, Shannon. ...My human days were happy too, with you as my goal, nurturing our friendship. ...Had I never known the pleasure of magic, never awakened as a witch, that would have continued.”
rows.jaText: 「さらばだ、紗音。……ニンゲンとして、そなたを目標に、そなたと友情を育みながらの日々も、楽しいものであったぞ。…もし妾が、魔法の悦楽を知ることなく、魔女に開眼することがなかったなら、それはこれからも変わらなかったであろうな」

ja:
………そなたにとっても、妾が唯一の親友であったな。
その親友が、忽然と消え去ることをどうか許してほしい。そなたへの置き土産として、……そなたの世界より、妾そのものを消し去る。今より、その部屋は二人部屋ではない。そなただけの、一人部屋である。そなたは、優しく、誰にも愛され、頼りにされる使用人を目指し、これからもそなたの理想の姿を体現していくが良い。もう、ヤスという、物をなくしてばかりの、愚かでドジな使用人は、存在しない。さらばだ、紗音。妾が魔女ベアトリーチェとして成熟し、夜の屋敷を自在に闊歩するようになれば。……夜の屋敷を見回るそなたと、やがては出会うこともあるだろう。しかし、そなたと再び出会う時。それは再会ではない。
それは、初めての出会いとなるのだ。何しろ、そなたは魔女ベアトリーチェの噂話は聞けど、会ったことなど、一度もないのだから……。さらばだ、紗音。いずれ出会い、何か面白い物語を紡ぎ合おうぞ………。
en:
...I was your only close friend too. Please forgive that friend's sudden disappearance.

As my parting gift to you, ...I erase myself from your world.

From now on, that room is not for two. It is a single room, yours alone.

Go on seeking to become a kind servant, loved and relied on by everyone. Go on embodying your ideal.

There is no longer a foolish, clumsy servant named Yasu, always losing things. Farewell, Shannon.

Once I have matured as the witch Beatrice and walk freely through the nighttime mansion, ...perhaps I shall meet you on your night rounds.

But when we meet again, it will not be a reunion. It will be our first meeting.

After all, you have heard rumors of the witch Beatrice, but never met her, not once... Farewell, Shannon.

Someday, let us meet and weave some interesting story together...

From now on, that room is not for two. It is a single room, yours alone. Go on seeking to become a kind servant, loved and relied on by everyone. Go on embodying your ideal. Once I have matured as the witch Beatrice and walk freely through the nighttime mansion, ...perhaps I shall meet you on your night rounds. But when we meet again, it will not be a reunion. It will be our first meeting. After all, you have heard rumors of the witch Beatrice, but never met her, not once... Farewell, Shannon. Someday, let us meet and weave some interesting story together...

ja:
………………………………。………私は、……何を…？寝惚けて、……たのかしら……？私は、自分の抜け出た寝床に向かって手を伸ばしながら、……待って、と言っていたようだった。寝惚けておかしなことを口走って、その勢いで目が覚めてしまった経験は、ないことはないけれど。……寝床を抜け出して、こうして立ったまま目が覚めた経験なんて、今までに一度もない。ひょっとしてこれが、……噂に聞く、夢遊病なのかしら…。私、疲れてる……？……寝なきゃ。寝直さなきゃ。私は、自分のベッドに、踵を返す。…………？振り返ったところで、自分のベッドなどそこにはない。
今、背を向けたベッドしか、この部屋にはないのだから。この部屋にいるのは私一人で、ベッドも私の背中に一つしかないなら……、……それはつまり、私のベッドということではないか。……なぜだか、釈然としない。ベッドの布団は、誰かが這い出たように、乱れている。誰かが這い出た…？　この部屋は、私の一人部屋じゃないか。なら、それは私のベッドであり、這い出た跡とはつまり、私がさっきまでこの布団に寝ていたということではないのか…？……でも、どうしてか、………このベッドが、……自分のベッドだと思えない。しかし、私、紗音は、他の子たちは相部屋なのに、私一人だけ一人部屋を与えられている。だから、ベッドも一つ。
無論、それは私のベッドのはず。
en:
................................ ...What ... was I...?

Had I ...been half asleep...?

Apparently, I'd been reaching toward the bed I'd climbed out of, ...saying, Wait.

I had talked nonsense in my sleep and woken myself up before. But I'd never climbed out of bed and woken up standing like this.

Perhaps this was ...that sleepwalking I'd heard about...

Was I tired...?

...I had to sleep. Go back to sleep.

I turned toward my bed. ...?

But when I turned, there was no bed there. The only bed in this room was the one I'd just turned away from.

If I was the only person here, and there was only one bed, behind me, ...then didn't that mean it was mine?

...Somehow, that didn't feel right.

The covers were rumpled, as though someone had crawled out. Someone had crawled out...? This was my single room, wasn't it? Then it was my bed, and the place where someone had crawled out meant ... I had been sleeping under those covers until a moment ago, didn't it...? ...But somehow, ... I couldn't feel ... that this bed was mine.

Yet I, Shannon, had been given a single room, while the other children shared. So there was only one bed. Of course, it had to be mine.

………………………………。………私は、……何を…？寝惚けて、……たのかしら……？私は、自分の抜け出た寝床に向かって手を伸ばしながら、……待って、と言っていたようだった。寝惚けておかしなことを口走って、その勢いで目が覚めてしまった経験は、ないことはないけれど。……寝床を抜け出して、こうして立ったまま目が覚めた経験なんて、今までに一度もない。ひょっとしてこれが、……噂に聞く、夢遊病なのかしら…。私、疲れてる……？……寝なきゃ。寝直さなきゃ。私は、自分のベッドに、踵を返す。…………？振り返ったところで、自分のベッドなどそこにはない。
今、背を向けたベッドしか、この部屋にはないのだから。この部屋にいるのは私一人で、ベッドも私の背中に一つしかないなら……、……それはつまり、私のベッドということではないか。……なぜだか、釈然としない。ベッドの布団は、誰かが這い出たように、乱れている。誰かが這い出た…？　この部屋は、私の一人部屋じゃないか。なら、それは私のベッドであり、這い出た跡とはつまり、私がさっきまでこの布団に寝ていたということではないのか…？……でも、どうしてか、………このベッドが、……自分のベッドだと思えない。しかし、私、紗音は、他の子たちは相部屋なのに、私一人だけ一人部屋を与えられている。だから、ベッドも一つ。
無論、それは私のベッドのはず。

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「………私、疲れてる、……のかな」
en: “... Am I ... tired...?”
rows.enText: “... Am I ... tired...?”
rows.jaText: 「………私、疲れてる、……のかな」

ja: きっと、寝惚けてるだけ。明日も学校が早い。そして、学校が終わったら、お屋敷に行って、少しお仕事の手伝いをしてから、熊沢さんとまた、読んだばかりの推理小説を語り合いたい。
en:
Surely I was just half asleep.

School started early tomorrow too. After school, I'd go to the mansion, help a little with the work, and then talk to Kumasawa again about the mystery I'd just read.

rows.speaker: Shannon
ja: 「寝よう。きっと、疲れてるからおかしなことを考えちゃうのね。………おやすみなさい、紗音。布団に包まれて、静かに目を閉じれば。……もう、何も難しいことは考えなくていいんだよ……」
en: “Let's sleep. I'm sure I'm thinking strange things because I'm tired. ...Good night, Shannon. Wrap yourself in the covers, quietly close your eyes. ...Then you won't have to think about anything difficult anymore...”

ja: 私は布団に潜り直す。自分のじゃない布団に潜ることに対する、わずかの嫌悪がチリチリとする。でも、だんだん眠くなってきたせいか、やはりこれは自分の布団だという気がしてきた。………私、寝惚けてるんだ……。
en:
I climbed back under the covers.

A little prickling aversion to getting into covers that weren't mine.

But perhaps because I was getting sleepy, gradually I began to feel they were mine after all.

...I was half asleep...

en:
I was Shannon. A servant, all alone. Sometimes I made mistakes, but ... I wanted to become a kind servant, loved by everyone...

...Good night.

...Me...

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: あぁ、我こそは我にして我等なり。もう使用人ごっこは飽きた。ニンゲンごっこは飽きた！これより我は、今宵より我はベアトリーチェ！千年を経た、黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェであるぞ！讃えよ使用人ども。怯えよ、夜回りに選ばれたることを！夜の島は屋敷は、全て妾のもの、妾の時間…！あぁ、我こそは我にして我等なり！さぁ、我等の世界にて全てを飲み込もう。それはまるで波濤のように！やれやれ、今夜もニンゲンの書物を肴に神秘の月を飲み干そう！これがミステリー？　これが密室？　これがニンゲンには不可能な犯罪とな？笑わせる！　その程度の隙だらけの穴だらけが、ニンゲンには不可能な犯罪とな！妾を感嘆させる素晴らしき密室魔法はないのか？あぁ、やれやれこれもこれも、それもあれも馬鹿らしい！くすりとは笑えるが、これでは月と書物の、どちらが肴かわからぬというもの！ミステリーに飽きれば、蝶に姿を変えて島を屋敷を！　広大な森を！　自由気ままに散歩しようではないか。臆病なる夜回りの使用人の後を、つけて回り、窓の戸締りを確かめる時、そのガラスに姿を映して肩越しに笑ってくれようぞ！何をするも自由自在、気ままで気紛れ！夜の悪戯はなかなかに楽しそうだ。よし、決めたぞ、今宵からはそれで遊ぼうぞ！くっくくくく、それは愉快！　今宵も愉快だ！魔女の世界は、想像力の限りの全てを遊べる！妾の想像力こそが、我が魔力の源なのだ！ならばよかろう、面白い！　それを無限大に広げようぞ。そしてそれで、島を全て飲み込んでやろうぞ。島の夜は全て妾のものなり！！あぁ、魔女の日々の何と優雅で愉快なることか！あぁ、我こそは我にして我等なり！　くっはははっはっはっは、ひゃっはっは！！愉快なる魔女の世界に、乾杯ッ！！
en:
Oh, I am I, and I am we.

I am tired of playing servant. Tired of playing human!

From now on, from this night, I am Beatrice! The thousand-year-old Golden Witch, Beatrice!

Praise me, servants. Tremble at being chosen for the night rounds!

The nighttime island, the mansion, all of it is mine. My time...! Oh, I am I, and I am we!

Come, let us swallow everything into our world. Like surging waves!

Well, well. Tonight too, let us drink down the mysterious moon, with human books to accompany it!

This is a mystery? This is a locked room? This is a crime impossible for humans?

Don't make me laugh! So many gaps, so many holes, and they call it impossible for humans!

Is there no magnificent locked-room magic to make me marvel?

Oh, dear me. This one, this one, that one, that one too. Ridiculous!

They can make me chuckle, but at this rate I can hardly tell which accompanies which, the moon or the book!

When we tire of mysteries, let us become butterflies and stroll freely through the island, the mansion, the vast forest!

Follow the timid servant on night rounds. When they check the windows are locked, appear in the glass and laugh over their shoulder!

Anything we do, freely, idly, capriciously!

Nighttime mischief looks quite delightful. Yes, I've decided. From tonight, that is how we shall play!

Heh heh heh. What fun! Tonight too, what fun!

In a witch's world, we can play with everything imagination holds! My imagination is the source of my magic!

Very well, then. How interesting! Let us expand it into infinity.

And with it, swallow the entire island.

The island's night is all mine!!

Oh, how graceful, how delightful, a witch's days!

Oh, I am I, and I am we! Heh hahahahahaha, hyahahaha!!

A toast to the delightful world of witches!!
